title: Fit a logistic regression with Newton's method
brief: Build the Hessian X^T D X + lambda I, a Newton step that solves H delta = g, and a fit loop that finishes in a handful of iterations where gradient descent needs hundreds.
hints: Let s = p * (1 - p) with p = sigmoid(X @ w). Then (X * s[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * np.eye(d) scales the rows of X without building a diagonal matrix.
newton_step returns delta = np.linalg.solve(hessian(...), gradient(...)). The caller subtracts it: w = w - delta.
fit_newton follows the descent loop: append the loss, compute the gradient, break if its norm is below tol, then step with the Newton delta.
Keep the small default ridge of 1e-8. It keeps np.linalg.solve from failing when two columns are copies of each other.
